body:
Substance: Alprazolam
Route: Oral
Dosage: 0.5 mg to 1.5 mg
Duration: Approximately 2 years
Setting: Home, work
Sex: Male
Body Weight: 153 lbs
Experience Type: Long-term use, taper, recovery
⸻
Started with 0.5 mg each night. Used it for sleep. Functional use, not recreational. I work in software. Clarity is required. It helped for a while. Then it started creating problems.
It helped for a while. Then it started creating problems.
The dose drifted. Occasionally 0.75 mg or more. Sometimes in the morning after drinking. Sometimes mid-day under pressure. I didnt enjoy it. I wasnt trying to. Eventually I noticed gaps. Slowed recall. Flat affect. Sloppy memory. I decided to taper.
Protocol was structured.

Each step lasted three days. Fifteen days total. Dosed nightly at the same time. I didnt introduce substitutes. No staggered reductions. No rechecks. The plan ran start to finish without deviation.
Diet was consistent. Steak, eggs, sardines. Supplements included magnesium glycinate, omega-3, creatine, and desiccated liver. Fluids were limited to water. No sugars. No processed food. No stimulants. No sedatives. I stayed home. Walked early in the morning. Maintained strict light and dark exposure.
Symptoms began immediately after the final dose. Sleep collapsed. Two hours per night at most. Shallow and broken. Cognition slowed. Chest tightness. Startle responses. The sense of being watched. Days stretched unnaturally long.
No psychosis. No seizure activity. No panic states. Discomfort was high but bounded. I maintained control by removing variables.
By day five, sleep extended. Four continuous hours. Cognitive function began to return around day seven. Emotional regulation followed. Appetite normalized. By day sixteen, sleep was stable. Six to eight hours, uninterrupted. By day twenty-one, baseline returned. Memory, energy, motivation, and clarity had reestablished.
Craving was absent. I was not tempted to resume. The drugs utility had run out. There was nothing left to seek.
I took no other medications. No adjuncts, prescriptions, or OTC interventions. No prior psychiatric diagnoses. No history of abuse patterns. No prior withdrawal events. I entered and exited clean.
Summary timeline:
Day 1: full sleep
Day 2: severe sleep collapse
Days 35: agitation, derealization
Day 6: first restoration of sleep
Day 7: cognitive function improving
Day 10: mood stabilization
Day 12: normal verbal clarity
Day 14: full affect restoration
Day 16: sleep consistent
Day 21: physical and mental baseline recovered
Supporting conditions:
Fixed taper
Isolated setting
Controlled inputs
Stable light cycles
Repetitive meals
Strict pacing
Absence of noise
Failures came from monitoring symptoms too closely. Recovery could not be accelerated. Mental loops made it harder. The trick was to ignore them.
Time distortion was present throughout. Days felt long. Improvement felt stalled even as it progressed. This resolved as sleep returned.
If exiting, set the plan and run it. Dont look back. Dont evaluate during discomfort. Wait. Then leave it behind.
